_note: PUBLIC-TIER structural patterns for credential-scan.mjs --tier public. These catch the GENERIC shapes by which a private system leaks into a public repo: note-app links, private-folder names, real user home paths, and email addresses. Nothing personal belongs in this file - it is tracked, and it ships inside the public slice alongside secure-push. Personal names, clients and local paths go in the PRIVATE deny-list (see public-denylist.example.json). Every pattern here is hard in the public tier. Use allowPaths (suffix match) for an intentional occurrence rather than weakening the regex.

patterns.name: wikilink
patterns._why: An Obsidian-style `link` is a pointer into the private knowledge base; it tells a reader the page exists and what it is called. Requires a letter and no leading space or $ so bash [[ -f x ]], nested arrays and code that GENERATES links ([[${name}]]) do not fire.

patterns.name: private-folder
patterns._why: Folder names that exist only in your private tree. Replace with yours: each one is a pointer into it.

patterns.name: private-root
patterns._why: Your private workspace root, by name. Replace with yours.

patterns.name: windows-user-home
patterns._why: A real Windows account name in a path. Generic placeholders (user, USERNAME, <...>, %USERNAME%, $USER) and single-character names are allowed.

patterns.name: posix-user-home
patterns._why: The same leak in Git Bash, macOS and Linux form. Single-character names (/Users/x) are test placeholders: a false positive measured on the live slice 2026-09-23.

patterns.name: email-address
patterns._why: PII. Test and placeholder domains, noreply senders and git@host SSH remotes are allowed.
